lines.text: Stuck on a big decision? Ask yourself ONE question.
lines.say: Stuck on a big decision? Ask yourself One question.

lines.text: Sam can't decide whether to quit his job. He's gone in CIRCLES for weeks.
lines.say: Sam can't decide whether to quit his job. He's gone in Circles for weeks.

lines.text: His neighbour Grace, a retired therapist, asks: what would you tell a FRIEND?
lines.say: His neighbour Grace, a retired therapist, asks: what would you tell a Friend?

lines.text: Sam answers instantly. Talk to your boss. Then DECIDE.
lines.say: Sam answers instantly. Talk to your boss. Then Decide.

lines.text: Researchers Grossmann and Kross found people reason more WISELY about a friend's problems than their own.
lines.say: Researchers Grossmann and Kross found people reason more Wisely about a friend's problems than their own.

lines.text: But picturing their own problem from the outside made the gap DISAPPEAR.
lines.say: But picturing their own problem from the outside made the gap Disappear.

lines.text: Next time you're stuck, ask it. Then take your own ADVICE.
lines.say: Next time you're stuck, ask it. Then take your own Advice.

post.title: Ask This When You're Stuck #shorts
post.description: Stuck on a decision? Ask what you'd tell a friend. Psychologists Igor Grossmann and Ethan Kross (Psychological Science, 2014) found people reason more wisely about a friend's relationship problem than their own — 'Solomon's paradox', after the king famed for wise advice and poor personal choices. When people reflected on their own problem from a distanced, third-person perspective, the gap disappeared. #psychology #shorts #decisionmaking #selfhelp
